messages.author: b7a46c53a2fcd90c
messages.subject: Facet_plot() distorts legends  and colorings
parts:
Hello,

I have a tree - tree1. 

With help of many people, but importantly of Yu, I managed to draw a nice tree plot that have 1. grouping of tips by geography. 2. desired colors of tip labels by the groups. 3. desired order of the keys in the legend. 4. added branches, drawn by dashed lines. 5. avoiding of drawing linetype legend.

When I make a facet_plot with geom_barh and tree1, all the colors of tree tips are changed and a legend for the linetype appears again. 

The question is - how to force facet_plot not to change the legends, which were thoroughly arranged in the previous stages. 

Best,
Hovhannes

Hello!

Thank you very much for answer.

I made a reproducible example with one of my published works about mitochondrial DNA haplogroup U7. I made a fake frequency table that was not in the paper. Fortunately, some of the problems are now resolved, but some are still there.

The R script and the tree files are attached. The _tree only.tiff is the drawing of pree3.

Today for the tree part the tip coloring and legend key order work fine. So the two problems are fixed now.

The problem of the addition of linetype legend is still there.

And additionally, it would be cool if there is a possibility to split the legends, control the coloring of the barplot part, and draw them separately onto their plots.

messages.author: b7a46c53a2fcd90c
messages.subject: Re: Facet_plot() distorts legends and colorings
parts:
Hi,

I just wanted to inform you about a small improvement. It was possible to get rid of linetype legend. Now the part looks like " + scale_linetype_manual(values = c("newly introduced" = "dashed", "original" = "solid"), guide=FALSE)".

Digging further.

Best,
Hovhannes

messages.author: 2a4584b898b0bd00
messages.subject: Re: Facet_plot() distorts legends and colorings
parts:
So the last problem is that you want to add legend separately in different facets?

This is not supported directly in ggplot2 and ggtree.

However, you can extract legend (e.g. using cowplot or grid) and use the legends as subplots to annotate the plot (e.g. using ggimage). This is out-of-scope of this group and you can find many examples in StackOverflow.
